title: Interspecies Pharmacokinetic Allometric Scaling Framework
description: Extrapolating clearance, volume of distribution, and elimination half-life from preclinical animal models (mice, rats, dogs, non-human primates) to adult humans using power-law models, physiological correction factors, and brain/body-weight adjustments. Serving as an international benchmark for first-in-human starting dose projection.
highlights: Pioneered simple and corrected allometric scaling formulas for biologics and small molecules
Evaluated species-specific predictive fidelity across 100+ pharmaceuticals
Widely recognized by regulatory reviewers for clinical trial IND safety margins

title: Pediatric and Neonatal Dose Optimization via Salisbury Rule
description: Addressing pediatric trial failures and underdosing/overdosing risks caused by empirical weight-based and body-surface-area (BSA) conversions. Establishing validation boundaries for the weight-based Salisbury Rule and GFR maturation algorithms across therapeutic proteins, neonates, and premature infants.
highlights: Demonstrated 0.5–1.5-fold clinical prediction accuracy across multiple pediatric cohorts
Bridged preterm neonatal clearance modeling with minimal PBPK architectures
Advised on pediatric clinical trial designs minimizing invasive blood draws

title: Biologics Pharmacokinetics: Coagulation Factors and Sparse Sampling
description: Designing robust sparse-sampling protocols (2–3 blood draws instead of traditional 10+ sampling points) to accurately estimate area under the curve (AUC) and clearance of recombinant factor VIII and factor IX in hemophilia patients without sacrificing statistical power or patient safety.
highlights: Alleviated sampling burden in vulnerable pediatric and adult hemophilia populations
Developed pharmacokinetic allometric scaling from animals to humans for 5 coagulation factors
Standardized review methodologies during 16-year tenure at FDA CBER
